summary: Twin granite towers on a bare rock off the entrance to Penobscot Bay, where teenager Abbie Burgess kept the lights burning through the gale of January 1856.

access.note: Island closed; bird-nesting sanctuary reachable only by boat or helicopter (Rowlett; USLHS).

facts.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (owner); U.S. Coast Guard operates the light

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree and the story says so: dwelling rebuilt 1846 (Heap, LighthouseFriends) vs 1847 (nomination, 1900 report); fog signal 1856 (Heap) vs 1869 (nomination) vs 1870 (LighthouseFriends); lens order (third in USLHS/Rowlett/LighthouseFriends vs second in the Board's 1890s reports); tower height 41 ft vs 48 ft; distance from mainland 18/20/25 miles; island area 25 vs 39 acres; Abbie Burgess's age (Heap 14 in 1853 and 17 in 1856, Putnam 14 in 1856; LighthouseFriends says 17). Heap also says the January 1856 gale destroyed Minot's Ledge Light and its keepers; that is wrong (Minot's Ledge fell in April 1851), so it was left out. Heap dates the 21-day skiff episode to spring 1857; LighthouseFriends is vague. The LHB 1892 passage (scan 375) is dated by position in the volume covering fiscal 1891 and 1892; the printed page is about 44 but unconfirmed, so scan pages are cited. The fog-signal appendix (scans 726, 753) is in the volume labelled 1893-94 and is cited by scan page. Facts taken only from LighthouseFriends (a modern compilation) are attributed to it in the text: 1826 appropriation and island purchase, Berry contract, 15 July 1827 first lighting, 1842 inspector and Abbott accounts, 1883/1888/1923 light changes, 1894 renovation, 1943 and 1950 items, Davis and Brackett remarks, 1983 lens removal, 1984 Audubon licence. NRHP listing year 1988 is from the station record and the nomination's January 1988 review date; the exact date was not read in the nomination. The OCR of the Grant passage (scan 753) is garbled, so it is paraphrased, not quoted. Roster rows come from the USLHS archive (NARA registers via Anderson); relationships among the Grants beyond what Heap and the Board say are not asserted. A 1926 Lighthouse Service Bulletin item (p. 167, PDF p. 50) records the Matinicus Rock keeper telephoning for a tender to help a disabled schooner off the station; the vessel's name is illegible in the OCR, so it is not used. The Commissioner's report for fiscal 1916 lists F. O. Hilt, second assistant keeper, in a table of rescues; the table is OCR-columnar and the act was not matched, so it is not used. Abbie's wedding year (1861) is Heap's; LighthouseFriends says 'before the year was out'. Photos were not collected. Checker 2026-10-22: Board 1892 report names no keeper; LighthouseFriends supplies 'Keeper Grant, 1890' and the roster shows the principal keeper changing in 1890 (John H. Grant to William G. Grant), so the story attributes the identification. 'Mr. I. Grant' (Board, 1894, p. 344) is matched to Isaac H. Grant only by initial, station pair and Heap's 1875 Whitehead move; the story says 'initial only'. James Anderson (LighthouseFriends) is matched to roster James M. Anderson (third assistant 1914-1917) by name and year, stated in the story. The Project Puffin site is on jacobtanenbaum.com; its affiliation with Audubon was not verified beyond its own text. Printed pages 317 and 344 were read from page images.
